simple_definition: How precisely each new layer of a chip lines up on top of the layers already printed.
technical_definition: Layer-to-layer alignment error of patterned features, typically specified in nm (e.g. ~0.7 nm claimed for EXE:5200B).

simple_definition: How many silicon wafers a lithography machine can expose in one hour; the main measure of its productivity.
technical_definition: Scanner throughput at a specified dose and field layout under the acceptance-test protocol (ATP); e.g. 220 wph NXE:3800E, 175 wph EXE:5200B.

simple_definition: A lithography machine that prints a chip pattern by sweeping a slit of light across the mask and wafer at the same time, then stepping to the next spot.
technical_definition: Step-and-scan exposure tool in which reticle and wafer stages move synchronously under a slit-shaped illumination field; standard for KrF, ArF, ArFi and EUV.

simple_definition: An older, simpler kind of lithography machine that exposes one whole chip area at a time and then moves (steps) to the next.
technical_definition: Step-and-repeat projection exposure tool exposing a full field at once; still common for i-line and packaging lithography.

simple_definition: The set of lenses or mirrors inside a lithography machine that shrinks the mask pattern and focuses it onto the wafer.
technical_definition: The projection optics (and associated illumination) module of a lithography system; for ASML supplied solely by Carl Zeiss SMT.

simple_definition: A very powerful laser that hits tiny drops of tin so they glow with the extreme ultraviolet light used in EUV machines.
technical_definition: Pulsed CO2 laser system (multi-stage amplifier, tens of kW average pulse power) used in laser-produced-plasma EUV sources; built by TRUMPF for ASML.

simple_definition: A gas laser that produces deep-ultraviolet light; it is the light source in DUV lithography machines.
technical_definition: Pulsed gas-discharge laser using rare-gas halide mixtures: KrF (248 nm) or ArF (193 nm); made by Cymer (ASML) and Gigaphoton (Komatsu).

simple_definition: Printing one very fine layer in two or more exposure steps because a single exposure cannot make features that small.
technical_definition: Splitting a layer's pattern across several litho-etch (or spacer) steps to beat a tool's single-exposure resolution; EUV and High-NA aim to replace some of these steps with one exposure.

simple_definition: Optics that shrink the mask image by different amounts in the two directions, used in High-NA EUV so existing mask sizes still work.
technical_definition: Projection optics with unequal demagnification (4x and 8x) in High-NA EUV, halving the exposure field and requiring field stitching for large dies.

simple_definition: A way of making chip patterns by pressing a patterned stamp into a soft coating on the wafer, instead of printing with light.
technical_definition: Jet-and-flash imprint of a template into resist, cured and released; Canon's FPA-1200NZ2C claims 14 nm minimum linewidth.

simple_definition: Lithography using 365-nanometre ultraviolet light from mercury lamps, for chips or layers that do not need very small features.
technical_definition: 365 nm mercury-lamp exposure (ASML lists ~220 nm resolution); dominant in power devices, MEMS, sensors and packaging.

simple_definition: Deep-ultraviolet lithography using 248-nanometre light from a krypton-fluoride laser.
technical_definition: 248 nm excimer-laser lithography (ASML lists ~80 nm resolution); used for mid-critical layers, notably in memory.

simple_definition: The most advanced kind of deep-ultraviolet lithography: 193-nanometre laser light with a thin layer of water between lens and wafer to print finer features.
technical_definition: 193 nm ArF excimer lithography with water immersion (NA up to 1.35, ~38 nm single-exposure resolution); ASML's NXT platform.

simple_definition: Testing a lithography machine at the maker's factory to prove it meets the agreed specification before it is shipped.
technical_definition: Pre-shipment test of an integrated system against contractual specs; ASML re-tests at site acceptance (SAT) after installation and recognises revenue at FAT for proven technologies.

simple_definition: Shipping a machine before all factory testing is done so the customer gets it sooner; final acceptance happens at the customer's site.
technical_definition: ASML practice of skipping some factory testing; revenue is deferred until site acceptance test when FAT acceptance is not proven.

simple_definition: An upgrade installed on a lithography machine already in a customer's factory to make it faster or more precise.
technical_definition: Post-sale system enhancement booked in ASML's installed base management (service and field option) revenue, e.g. NXE:3800E upgrades in 2025.

simple_definition: Using computer models to pre-distort the patterns on a mask so they print correctly on the wafer.
technical_definition: Algorithms and process models (e.g. OPC) that optimise reticle patterns and process windows for given lithography conditions.

simple_definition: An older lithography machine that is reconditioned and resold, often to makers of mature chips.
technical_definition: Pre-owned scanner/stepper resold after refurbishment; reported separately by ASML (used systems) and Nikon (refurbished units).

simple_definition: How much lithography (and spending on it) a chipmaker needs for each wafer it makes; it rises as chips get more advanced.
technical_definition: ASML term for litho exposures or litho spend per wafer start; a driver in its 2030 scenarios.
